card.name: Words just before oxygen or acid-drug terms
card.fires_on: Short words or word starts right before a drug or therapy term, such as 'low' before flow oxygen, 'like' before omeprazole, or a comma after famotidine. Seen in drug-interaction and toxicity-grading text.

modes.label: Low-flow oxygen
modes.description: The word 'low' after 'hypoxia requiring' in fever and low blood pressure grading criteria.
modes.example: Hypoxia requiring<< low>>-flow oxygen Low-flow oxygen defined as oxygen

modes.label: Acid-reducer context
modes.description: Linking words or punctuation next to PPI or H2 blocker names like famotidine and omeprazole.
modes.example: PPI therapy<< like>> Omeprazole and Sodium Bic

modes.label: Instruction verbs
modes.description: Start of an action verb in a dosing or test instruction.

card.plain: It fires on small words that come just before a named drug or oxygen term, mostly in acid-reducer and fever-grading text.
